alternative_explanations.explanation: The 49.64% on the single vfmv.f.s fa0,v2 line may include PMU skid / imprecise-IP alignment from the preceding vfredosum.vs and vsetvli instructions rather than pure reduction latency. The robust observation is interval-level: the three control/config/reduction groups jointly absorb ~88% of samples while vfmul.vv/vfredosum FP math is ~0.8%.

A memory-bound explanation (unit-stride vle8.v/vle32.v loads stalling) is contradicted by perf stat: L1_dcache_load_miss_rate 0.645% and LLC_load_miss_rate 0.202%, so the loop is latency/control-bound, not cache-bound.

Loop branch (bnez 14.17%) and pointer-advance (add 3.29%) overhead could be claimed as the dominant cause alone; but they are linear per-iteration costs that reduce proportionally when LMUL is raised, so they are symptoms of the 4-element-per-iteration structure rather than an independent cause.

findings.conclusion: In faiss::scalar_quantizer::DCTemplate<Quantizer8bitDirectSigned<6>,SimilarityIP<6>,NONE>::query_to_code/compute_distance, the compiler-auto-vectorized RVV inner-product loop runs at LMUL e8/mf4 (4 code bytes per iteration on the zvl128b build target) and performs a per-block ordered vfredosum with a scalar-register-file accumulator round-trip, making the loop latency/control-bound: block reduction+config+branch instructions absorb ~88% of samples (vfmv.f.s 49.64%, vsetvli/vsetivli 28.2%, bnez 14.17%) while the FP multiply work is ~0.5%.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Row gate fails: LMUL is not at its legal/measured optimum (e8/mf4 remote from the spill-free frontier), so that row explicitly defers to register-group sizing first; fixed-LMUL unroll enumeration is premature.
The vfmv.s.f scalar accumulator broadcast is consumed by vfredosum.vs, which has no scalar operand (vx/vi) form; no operand-form substitution exists for this loop.
The loop uses ta/ma everywhere with no tu/mu, no mask clearing, and no preserved tail lanes; liveness/policy evidence is absent.
That row is restricted to Go byte-processing main loops (vle8/vse8 copies/compares); this is a C++ numeric distance loop, not a byte-processing kernel.
The loop is plain compiler autovectorization of a scalar C++ loop (distance_computers.h:34-39), not a handwritten intrinsic kernel disturbed by autovec; no -fopt-info-vec/Rpass evidence.

findings.reasoning: Distance-computers.h compute_distance is a scalar reduction loop (acc += q[i]*reconstruct(code,i)) auto-vectorized by the RISC-V backend. Disassembly at 0x7aae4c-0x7aae8a processes only 4 bytes per iteration (vsetvli a5,a4,e8,mf4; VLMAX=e8/mf4=4 on VLEN128). Per iteration it runs an ordered vfredosum.vs and round-trips the accumulator through the FP scalar register file (0x7aae5c vfmv.s.f, 0x7aae86 vfmv.f.s), plus 4 vsetvl-family instructions (0x7aae4c, 0x7aae58 vsetivli VL=1, 0x7aae60 restore 24.98%, 0x7aae6c SEW switch). Aggregate of the top hot lines in the loop interval: 49.64+24.98+3.18+14.17+3.29 = ~95.3% while actual FP work (0x7aae7e vfmul.vv 0.47%, 0x7aae82 vfredosum.vs 0.36%) is <1%. Loop is serialized by a 4-element ordered reduction on the loop-carried critical path. mf4 is below the legal LMUL frontier; live set is only v1..v4, so e8/m1..m8 and unroll candidates are spill-free territory. This is the rvv_register_group_utilization failure form (LMUL below frontier -> excessive iterations of vsetvl, reduction round-trip, and branch).

alternative_explanations.explanation: The ordered vfredosum.vs was likely chosen to preserve exact FP accumulation order; converting to merge-once-end vector-accumulator form changes addition association and may need a -ffast-math/contract or documented last-bit tolerance. The mechanism (per-chunk reduction serialization) still holds under that contract caveat.

Part of the 49.64% at vfmv.f.s fa0,v2 could be charged to the immediately preceding vsetvli restore stall rather than the reduction dependency itself; with sampling-IP precision unmeasured (baseline_gap), the split between reduction-latency and config-latency is uncertain. The combined conclusion that per-block horizontal reduction round-tripping dominates is preserved.

The vfmv.s.f/vsetivli VL=1 broadcast before each vfredosum could be considered a separate dictional-form issue; however no scalar-operand vfredosum form exists, so the round-trip removal must go through keeping a vector accumulator across the loop rather than an operand-form substitution.

findings.conclusion: A contributing factor is the per-block horizontal reduction: vfredosum.vs + vfmv.f.s fa0 (49.64%) + next-iteration vfmv.s.f round-trips the accumulator through the FP scalar register file on the loop-carried critical path for every 4-element block, serializing reduction latency instead of keeping vector accumulators that are merged once at the end.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: No nested M/N/K loops, GEMV/microkernel structure, or packing exists; compute_distance is a single standalone dot-product-style accumulation, which the reduction row explicitly retains ('dot-product-like additive accumulation as a standalone reduction without matmul microkernel structure').
The vsext.vf4+vfcvt.f.x.v chain is semantically required (int8 -> float reconstruction) and samples ~0%; it is not the bottleneck.
Work is in the FP domain (vfcvt to float, vfmul.vv, vfredosum) with no Int32 accumulator, zero-point, multiplier/shift requantization, or narrowing.
The loop has a cross-element accumulator (vfredosum.vs v2,v1,v2), which that row's exclusion routes to the corresponding reduction row.

findings.reasoning: The loop executes a horizontal reduction for every 4-element block: 0x7aae82 vfredosum.vs v2,v1,v2 then 0x7aae86 vfmv.f.s fa0,v2 extracts to scalar, next iteration 0x7aae5c vfmv.s.f v2,fa0 re-splats. This places the sequential 4-adder reduction on the loop-carried critical path every 4 elements, which rvv_widening_reduction_kernels section 9 explicitly names as a failure form ('executes vfred* for every chunk and immediately extracts the result to a scalar serializes horizontal-reduction latency and vector-to-scalar transfer on the loop-carried critical path'); its fix is to retain multiple independent vector accumulators and merge once at the end. Source semantics (distance_computers.h:34-39) confirm a standalone dot-product-like additive accumulation with no matmul microkernel, so widening-reduction ownership excludes rvv_floating_point_matmul_and_gemv_kernels.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The vsetivli zero,1,e32,m1 at 0x7aae58 is functionally required by the vfmv.s.f v2,fa0 broadcast; the 0x7aae60 vsetvli restore is thus a true state re-establishment after a real state change, not dead code. Elimination requires removing the broadcast (vector accumulator across the loop) or restructuring, not merely deleting the vsetvli.

The repeated vsetvli churn could be attributed to the LMUL/SEW design (e8/mf4 -> e32/m1 conversion forces SEW and VL restarts each block) and thus owned by the register-group pattern rather than an independent emitter state-tracking defect; both interpretations agree the per-iteration config overhead should shrink.

On a wider-LMUL rebuild, absolute vsetvli cost per element may already drop; thesis then becomes that config overhead is proportional to iteration count rather than an orthogonal defect. rvv_vector_state_management would then not be primary at all.

findings.conclusion: A contributing factor is per-iteration vector-state re-establishment: each 4-element block executes 4 vsetvl-family instructions including a 24.98%-sampled vsetvli restore of the same e8/mf4 config at 0x7aae60 (undone only by the vsetivli VL=1 broadcast helper at 0x7aae58), contributing roughly a quarter of the function's samples.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: Part of the config churn is a consequence of the e8/mf4->e32/m1 SEW/LMUL split of the chosen lowering; the register-group pattern owns that slice and remains primary for the root cause.
The vsetivli VL=1 dance serves the vfmv.s.f scalar-to-vector seed; no vx/vi replacement exists for a vfredosum seed, so operand-form selection is not the mechanism.

findings.reasoning: Four vsetvl-family instructions execute every iteration: 0x7aae4c vsetvli a5,a4,e8,mf4 (compute VL), 0x7aae58 vsetivli zero,1,e32,m1 (VL=1 for broadcast), 0x7aae60 vsetvli zero,a5,e8,mf4 (re-assert the identical config; 24.98% of samples), 0x7aae6c vsetvli zero,zero,e32,m1 (SEW switch).
